refined_spec.refined_prompt:
## APPARENTLY LAW — Site Build (MVP)

### Project Scope
Build a professional, marketing-focused website for Apparently Law, a sister law firm entity that:
- Serves as the default escalation destination for legal matters
- Acts as the anchor of the boutique lawyer network under Apparently OS
- Displays network member firms and handles matter routing to appropriate specialists

This is NOT building Apparently OS (the practice operating system platform)—only the Apparently Law firm's own website.

### Technology Stack
- **Framework**: Nuxt 4 (integrate with existing `/Users/kpasch/Documents/apparently` codebase)
- **Backend**: Supabase (existing project)
- **Hosting**: Vercel (existing project)
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS (existing in stack)
- **CMS/Content**: Supabase PostgreSQL for case studies, team bios, pricing tiers
- **Analytics**: Vercel Analytics (integrated)

### MVP Feature Set (v1 — blocking acceptance)
1. **Landing Page** — hero, value prop, boutique network overview, CTA
2. **Services Page** — primary practice areas (transactional, dispute resolution, IP, etc.)
3. **Team Page** — founding partner(s) bio(s), credentials, headshots from Supabase
4. **Pricing & Engagement** — transparent tier display (boutique-friendly, subscription models), NOT full Stripe integration (display only, see v1.5 below)
5. **Boutique Network Directory** — table/grid of network member firms (name, location, specialty, contact) sourced from Supabase
6. **Contact & Matter Intake** — inquiry form, sends to team email via Resend (already in stack)
7. **Case Studies/Testimonials** — 3–5 examples, CMS-editable via Supabase
8. **Mobile-responsive design** — tested on iOS + Android (see test plan)
9. **Accessibility** — WCAG 2.1 AA minimum (law firms have legal liability for exclusion)
10. **SEO fundamentals** — meta tags, structured data (schema.org), robots.txt, sitemap (critical for law firm discovery)

### Deferred to v1.5+ (NOT blocking MVP)
- Full Stripe payment integration (tokenization, invoicing)
- Client portal / authentication (login, matter tracking)
- Email notification workflows (matter status updates)
- Analytics dashboard (matter pipeline tracking)

### Legal & Compliance Requirements
- **Attorney-Client Privilege**: Do NOT store privileged communications in Supabase (intake form is informational only, not privileged)
- **Data Privacy**: GDPR compliance, privacy policy, cookie banner (inquiry data is non-personal unless user chooses to share; no storage of SSN, financial data)
- **Bar Compliance**: Verify no unauthorized practice of law (site is informational, not legal advice)
- **Contact Info**: Office address, phone, licensed attorney name(s) must be displayed per state bar rules
- **Disclaimer**: "This is not legal advice" footer on all pages

### End Users (Persona)
Potential clients seeking specialized legal services; also existing network members browsing boutique directory.

### Performance & Availability SLOs
- Page load (Largest Contentful Paint): < 2.5s on 4G
- Uptime: 99.5% (standard Vercel SLA)
- Lighthouse score: ≥ 90 on mobile, ≥ 95 on desktop

### Content Ownership & Process
- **Owner approval gate**: Legal content (attorney bios, services descriptions, disclaimers, case studies) requires operator review before deploy
- **No public authentication v1**: Owner-only access to edit content via Supabase Studio or simple admin panel (defer full CMS to v1.5)

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 10 MVP features deployed and tested in staging
- [ ] WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility audit passes (`npm run a11y:check` clean)
- [ ] Lighthouse mobile ≥ 90, desktop ≥ 95
- [ ] E2E tests for landing, services, contact form (see `/test/e2e/*.spec.ts`)
- [ ] SEO checklist: meta tags, Open Graph, structured data, sitemap, robots.txt
- [ ] Legal review: disclaimer, privacy policy, attorney credentials visible
- [ ] Case studies CMS schema defined in Supabase and populated (2+ examples)
- [ ] Boutique directory synchronized with network member list (Supabase table schema defined)
- [ ] Contact form → Resend email working end-to-end
- [ ] Vercel preview deployment stable for 1 week, zero P1 logs

### Repository & Deployment
- **Source repo**: `apparently` (at `/Users/kpasch/Documents/apparently`; already exists)
- **New branch**: `feature/law-site-mvp` off `main`
- **Staging deploy**: Vercel preview (auto on PR)
- **Production route**: Auto-merge to `main` after tests pass, then batch-train merge-to-prod (see orchestrator rules)
- **Vercel project**: Existing (confirm with operator before activation)
- **Supabase project**: Existing (confirm schema migrations applied before feature development)

### Blocking Prerequisites (Operator must complete)
- [ ] Verify Vercel project exists and is linked to `apparently` repo
- [ ] Verify Supabase project exists and is linked (env vars `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` in Vercel)
- [ ] Create Supabase tables: `team_members`, `case_studies`, `boutique_directory` (schema templates provided by implementer)
- [ ] Operator registers project in orchestrator intake (create PROMPT-apparently-law.md in dropbox to auto-activate)

### Success Metrics
- Site indexed by Google within 2 weeks
- Organic search traffic for practice-area keywords (e.g., "San Francisco venture capital law")
- Contact form submissions logged (Resend + Supabase audit logs)
- Boutique directory updated and accurate (weekly sync)
- No accessibility or SEO regression from existing apparently codebase

### Cross-Learning Context
⚠️ **NOTE**: Original spec included truncated remediation-loop feedback unrelated to this task; removed. This is a standalone site-build task with no dependency on orchestrator remediation loops.
